title: A Preliminary Study by Carl Haag
content: In this preliminary study for a bridal procession, Carl Haag uses the camel's eye as the vanishing point of the scene. The eye level of the viewer is drawn horizontally through that point. That line describes a plane about eight feet above the ground, approximately two feet above the heads of standing adult figures.Sketch for the lower half of A Bridal Procession at Damascus,Haag, Carl R.W.S (1820 - 1915), Syria (drawn) ca. 1892 (drawn)Using pen and ink for studies is a method that goes back to the old masters. The shadow values are suggested with simple brown washes. It's a good practice because it forces you to commit to an idea and see it through.Carl Haag, Wedding procession in DamascusWhen it comes to doing the final painting, you may choose a completely different idea.
